title: Post-Radiotherapy Brain Metastasis Longitudinal Review
summary: Align serial brain MRI follow-up after radiotherapy, summarize interval lesion response, and prepare a concise clinician-facing review brief.
clinical_goal: Determine whether the treated brain metastasis appears stable, responsive, or concerning across longitudinal MRI follow-up and package the result into a review-ready physician brief.
problem_statement: Longitudinal neuro-oncology follow-up often requires manual alignment of serial MRI, treatment timing, and interval response language before a clinician can confidently finalize the review.

inputs.name: longitudinal_series_catalog
inputs.description: Serial brain MRI studies with sequence labels, dates, and privacy-preserving derived assets.

inputs.name: treatment_timeline
inputs.description: Treatment timing used to align response review with the imaging timeline.

inputs.name: radiomics_snapshot
inputs.description: Derived lesion burden values or equivalent longitudinal response measurements.

inputs.name: clinical_context
inputs.description: Compact clinical context such as histology, lesion location, and intervention.

sample_queries: Review this longitudinal brain MRI follow-up and draft a physician summary.
Does the latest follow-up suggest treatment response or concerning progression?
Prepare a concise tumor board brief for this treated brain metastasis case.

rule_sets.summary: Align treatment timing, longitudinal imaging, and response trend before drafting the clinician-facing brief.
Prepare a concise draft review and preserve human sign-off whenever the longitudinal signal remains clinically meaningful.

actions.label: Create longitudinal review item
actions.description: Queue the case for clinician sign-off after automated synthesis.

actions.label: Draft physician brief
actions.description: Prepare a compact longitudinal neuro-oncology review summary.

examples: Compare this treated brain metastasis across serial MRI follow-up and draft a tumor board brief.
Summarize the treatment-aligned trend and the current concern for this longitudinal MRI case.
